brief.headline: Offer to pay in 15 days (freeing ₹26.60 L of our cash) in exchange for a ~12% price cut—their cash is stuck for 101 days and they borrow at 12.16%, so early payment is worth that rate to them.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for an 11–12% price cut if we pay in 15 days instead of 30.
priceAsk.target: A discount worth roughly their 12.16% borrowing rate, applied to the ₹26.60 L we'd pay 15 days earlier each year.
priceAsk.basis: Their cash is stuck for 101 days—much longer than similar firms (64 days)—and they borrow money at 12.16%. Paying them 15 days faster is worth that rate to them, so we should share the saving. Our current price sits at the top of the fair market band (₹250/kg typical for pharma sachets, market asks ₹205–305/kg), so there's room to move down.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Propose paying in 15 days (instead of 30) in return for the price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹26.60 L of our cash, but the price cut should more than cover that cost for us.

brief.financialLeverage: Shrinath Roto keeps only 2.3% of every ₹100 they sell as profit, and they owe 1.25 times their own cash (₹282.62 Cr in debt). Their cash is stuck for 101 days—way longer than similar firms (64)—so cash is very tight for them, and they borrow at 12.16%. We're 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue, so not a make-or-break customer, but their Altman Z-score is 2.36 (grey zone—neither safe nor distressed) and they've had EPF payment delays, so push firmly on price-for-speed but don't squeeze so hard we destabilise supply. Lead with the win-win: faster cash for them, lower price for us.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck much longer than peers
They borrow money at a high rate
They carry a lot of debt relative to their own cash
They've had delays paying into the staff provident fund

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volumes—proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets; qualify for larger orders.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant that makes both the film substrate and converts it—can second-source at scale; send RFQ to benchmark price and lead time.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter specialising in pharma blister and sachet laminates; strong second-source candidate (health score D 31/100, so verify financials before committing large volumes).

risks: Their Altman Z-score is 2.36 (grey zone—neither clearly safe nor in distress) and they've had EPF payment delays, so watch supply continuity closely and don't push so hard the supplier tips over.
They keep only 2.3% profit, so a very aggressive price cut could hurt their ability to deliver consistently—balance the price ask with the payment-speed offer.
We're just 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue, so we have less clout than with smaller suppliers—line up Huhtamaki or UFLEX as a credible Plan B before the meeting.
Credit rating is CARE BBB+ / Stable (middling)—consider capping our exposure and formally qualifying a second source this quarter.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to help free up your cash by paying in 15 days instead of 30—and in return, we're looking for an 11–12% price reduction that reflects the 12.16% you're paying to borrow.
